brief: A planter for a sunny kitchen windowsill with three herbs growing in it.

requirements.evidence: 3 full hex bases (piece 0,-1 / 0,0 / 0,1) each holding a drained full-depth bin (hex-bin-full-drain) filled with soil.

A single straight row along the sill: 501 mm long, 191 mm deep, 80 mm tall without plants (about 180 mm with them). The two joints between bases are fastened with joint bolts (jointBolt:0#0,-1#5 and jointBolt:0#0,1#2). I can't see your sill, so check that 191 mm of depth fits it.
basil-young, parsley-young and chives-young are planted, one per bin. No PLANT_NOT_IN_SOIL or other prop warnings.

requirements.requirement: Copes with a sunny window (sun/UV and heat resistance)
requirements.evidence: The configurator checks only fit and collisions, not sun or heat resistance. That depends on the filament you print with.

requirements.requirement: Watering and drainage on a kitchen sill
requirements.evidence: The bins have drain holes, but the build has no drip tray. The configurator can't check whether it's waterproof, so put a saucer under it or use some other way to protect the sill.

finish.summary: The planter is a straight row of three joined hex bases, each holding a drained full-depth bin of soil, 501 × 191 × 80 mm. It has basil, flat-leaf parsley and chives growing in it, one per bin. check_build reports no rule errors and the meshes are clear. Parts list: 6 printed parts (about 1.18 kg of filament) plus 8 M6 screws and 8 nuts. Sun/UV and heat resistance depend on the material and can't be checked here. There's no drip tray to catch water from the drain holes.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: A windowsill planter: a straight row of three cells, each with a deep bin. Let me see piece sockets and bins.
